item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00328","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C15","C06","C24"],"selected_candidate_label":"C15","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C15 is the immediately preceding annual Cancer Control Month proclamation and plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. The child preserves its recital sequence—cancer mortality, preventability through existing knowledge and treatment, public education, coordinated public-private efforts, and annual statutory authorization—and closely follows its operative provisions designating April, inviting gubernatorial proclamations, and mobilizing the medical profession and communications industries. C06 is another strong earlier iteration of substantially the same template but is more remote. C24 shares language about coordinated public and private action for prevention and control, but not enough distinctive machinery to qualify independently.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas more than a third of these lives could probably be saved, and many others prolonged, if full use were made of our present knowledge of cancer","parent_excerpt":"Whereas according to the best medical opinion a large number of cancer deaths could be prevented if full use were made of our present knowledge concerning early diagnosis and treatment of the disease","explanation":"Distinctive parallel statement that many cancer deaths are preventable through full use of existing knowledge."},{"child_excerpt":"Whereas by Public Resolution 82, 75th Congress, approved March 28, 1938 (52 Stat. 148), the President is authorized and requested to issue annually a proclamation setting apart the month of April of each year as Cancer Control Month","parent_excerpt":"Whereas by a joint resolution approved March 28, 1938 (52 Stat. 148), the Congress authorized and requested the President to issue annually a proclamation setting apart the month of April as Cancer Control Month","explanation":"The child closely reproduces the same statutory recital and annual proclamation mechanism."},{"child_excerpt":"do hereby set apart the month of April 1950 as Cancer Control Month, and I invite the Governors of the States, Territories, and possessions of the United States to issue proclamations for the same purpose","parent_excerpt":"do hereby set apart the month of April 1949 as Cancer Control Month; and I invite the Governors of the several States and the Territories and possessions of the United States to issue similar proclamations","explanation":"The core operative provision is nearly identical, with only the year and minor wording changed."},{"child_excerpt":"I also urge the medical profession, the press, the radio and motion-picture industries, and all interested agencies and individuals to unite during April 1950 in public dedication to a program for the control of cancer","parent_excerpt":"I also invite the medical profession, the press, the radio, the motion-picture industry, and all organizations and individuals interested in a national program for the control of cancer by education and other cooperative means to unite during the month of April in a public dedication to this program","explanation":"The child reuses the parent's distinctive list of mobilized professions and media and the call to unite in an April public dedication."}]}
